documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning about a red sore patch on her right shin since Sunday; seen same day.

No injury she remembers, dry skin from the cold. Area warm and tender, spreading a little since yesterday. No chills. Not using filgrastim lately.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right anterior lower leg with a blanching, warm, tender area of erythema about 8 x 6 cm, margins marked with pen. No fluctuance, no drainage, no streaking. No inguinal nodes. Calf soft. Left leg normal.

CBC today: WBC 2.3, ANC 0.9.

A/P: nonpurulent cellulitis, right lower leg, in a neutropenic patient on methotrexate and prednisone.
- Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily x 7 days. Sulfa antibiotics excluded (anaphylaxis).
- ANC under 1000: called hematology - they advise she use her filgrastim per her standing instructions; she has syringes at home.
- Elevate, moisturize the skin.
- If the redness passes the pen line, or fever, call immediately - low threshold for ED.
Phone check in 48 hours.

documents.body: Called pt. Redness inside the pen marks and less warm. No fever. Taking cephalexin, used filgrastim Tuesday night per hematology. Will finish course.

documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called at 8 with three days of cough and feeling feverish; seen this morning.

Cough productive, tired, some right-sided chest discomfort with deep breaths. Felt hot overnight. No hemoptysis. Third infection this year after the two leg cellulitis episodes (January here, March at an urgent care).

Exam: vitals as charted, not in distress, speaking full sentences. Crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart regular. Leg skin healed bilaterally.

CXR done in house: right lower lobe consolidation (see report). CBC: WBC 2.5, ANC 1.1.

A/P:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, RLL, outpatient-treatable today (oxygenating well, eating and drinking, has support by phone). Levofloxacin 750 mg daily x 5 days - she is sulfa-anaphylactic; reviewed tendon precautions with the prednisone. Call or go to the ED for breathlessness, confusion, or not improving in 48-72 hours.
2. Recurrent infections with Felty neutropenia - three in four months. Referral to hematology for an earlier visit than the routine summer one; note sent.
3. Left leg cellulitis from March resolved.
RN check-in Monday. Recheck visit in about 6 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Airspace consolidation in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal. Left lung clear.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks after RLL pneumonia. Feels back to baseline - cough gone, no fevers. Working her regular shifts.

Exam: afebrile, sat normal on room air. Lungs clear throughout, including the right base. Spleen tip palpable.

A/P: pneumonia resolved clinically; no repeat film needed at this point. Hematology 7/20 for recurrent infections. Low threshold to be seen for any fever. Next routine visit late summer.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Admission 06/14/2026 - Discharge 06/16/2026
Service: Internal Medicine

Reason for admission: evaluation of repeated infections in a neutropenic patient.

History: 58-year-old woman with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and Felty syndrome (chronic neutropenia, splenomegaly). Over the past half year she has had two episodes of lower-leg cellulitis (January, March) and a right lower lobe pneumonia in April, each treated as an outpatient. She presented through the emergency department for evaluation of this pattern. Her arthritis is currently quiet on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone.

PMH: as above; glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis; chronic fatigue syndrome. PSH: bilateral carpal tunnel release; bone marrow biopsy and splenic aspiration 2021.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Exam on admission: afebrile, BP 130/80, HR 78, RR 16. No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Joints without synovitis; chronic deformities of longstanding RA in the hands. Palpable spleen tip. Skin intact, no cellulitis.

Data: Hgb 12.5, WBC 2.1, ANC 0.8, platelets 180. RF positive, ACPA positive. CMP unremarkable. Blood cultures x2: no growth. CXR: clear, prior RLL opacity resolved.

Hospital course: no active infection identified. Hematology consulted; filgrastim 300 mcg given on 6/14 and 6/15 with ANC 1.9 (WBC 3.4) on 6/16. Given the frequency of infections on as-needed dosing, hematology recommended scheduled filgrastim twice weekly. Rheumatology aware; no change to methotrexate or prednisone.

Discharge medications:
- Filgrastim 300 mcg SC twice weekly (Mon/Thu) - CHANGED from as needed
- Methotrexate 20 mg weekly
- Prednisone 5 mg daily
- Folic acid 1 mg daily except methotrexate day
- Risedronate 35 mg weekly
- Calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 600 mg/400 IU twice daily

Follow-up: PCP within one week; hematology 7/20 as scheduled. Return for temperature 38.0 C or higher.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know she was in the hospital Sunday to Tuesday. Went in through the ED Sunday afternoon because she was worried about all the infections. Told no infection right now; they gave her filgrastim shots and her count came up, and she is to take it twice a week now instead of only when called. No discharge papers sent to us yet - requested. Feels fine, afebrile. Has syringes; specialty pharmacy shipping more. Post-hospital visit booked Monday 6/22.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital 6/14-6/16 for evaluation of recurrent infections; summary not received yet, history from patient and her discharge med sheet.

Per patient: no infection found, cultures negative so far, chest film clear. Got filgrastim two days and her neutrophils rose. Discharged on filgrastim twice weekly (Mon/Thu). Gave herself this morning's dose without trouble. No fevers.

Med reconciliation: filgrastim changed from as-needed to 300 mcg twice weekly - list updated. Methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg, folic acid, risedronate, calcium/D unchanged.

Exam: afebrile, well. Lungs clear. Spleen tip palpable. Skin intact on both legs.

A/P: Felty syndrome with recurrent infections, now on scheduled growth factor. Hematology 7/20. No NSAIDs. Fever 100.4 or higher: call us any hour. Follow-up late summer.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Seen 07/20/2026.

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Kelleher after her June admission. Since discharge she has had no fevers or infections. She is injecting filgrastim 300 mcg Mondays and Thursdays without difficulty.

Exam: well-appearing. Spleen tip palpable. No adenopathy. Skin intact.
CBC: WBC 2.9, ANC 1.4, hemoglobin 12.3, platelets 175.
Medications: filgrastim 300 mcg SC twice weekly; methotrexate 20 mg weekly; prednisone 5 mg daily; folic acid; risedronate 35 mg weekly; calcium/vitamin D3.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Assessment: Felty syndrome with improved neutrophil count on scheduled filgrastim.
Plan: continue twice-weekly filgrastim. CBC with differential in one month - fine to draw at your office and send to us. I will see her again in three months.

Hematology & Oncology
